study.question: Can within-group saturation of repeated fine-age bins improve the cheap history representation, and does any effect depend on localization to target-match groups?
study.hypothesis: Observation: local_product achieved AUC .6200553701 with train419.85s versus frozen joint_identity .6204259428 with train548.36s. Replacing local fine ages by a coarse-conditional factorization reduced AUC to .6198326327; the same localization contrast with joint identities was .6200881087 versus .6195933663. These are single-seed observations, not established mechanisms. The latest fine action-age interaction failed to improve AUC: observed .6199866501 versus conditional .6200742330 and parent .6200553701, despite better Logloss. Proposed explanation: repeated events concentrated in one fine-age bin may dominate the linear mean before 16-dimensional compression, obscuring less frequent periods. Replace only fine-recency weights p_k=N_k/N by q_k=log(1+N_k)/sum_j log(1+N_j). Both are unit mass for nonempty groups, retain the same fine-bin support, and give zero for empty groups. Keep action means and explicit coarse tables unchanged. Predict useful redistribution rather than an added action-age interaction or increased neural capacity. This is a provisional implementation question, not a verified new method. Trajectory review: the first compact_summary and compact_matched reached .6191293980 and .6195180296, so added active capacity recovered only part of the deficit. compact_pair_fold (.6195645269) exceeded compact_matched, while reference_pair_fold (.6201173013) fell below joint_identity: this mixed pairing evidence does not establish event binding as the reference mechanism. pooled_content (.6194305134) trailed fine_context (.6200897204), and coarse_reencode (.6196349149) did not match fine_context; these exploratory branches motivate preserving fine ages rather than restoring all content pooling. The latest action-age branch is retained as a negative primary-metric trajectory. All supplied trial statuses are success and previous_runtime_error is null; no unavailable or failed execution is invented.

study.proposed_difference: One readout intervention: normalize log1p fine-age bin counts before multiplying by the existing recency embedding dictionary, keeping action means separate and unchanged. Factorial switch crosses concave versus empirical-mean weighting with local versus coarse-conditional fine recency. All four modules allocate identical parameters in identical order; normalization adds no trainable parameters, event embedding path, labels, optimizer or auxiliary objective. The mean branches reproduce their existing parent arithmetic exactly. Nonlinear count aggregation differs from event-mean compression and from the unsuccessful fine action-age cross-moment branch. Search of authorized paper/agent indices for histogram, temporal, summary and fine returned no further nearest methods; novelty outside inspected sources remains unverified.
predictions: Implementation: mean_local must reproduce parent local_product representation and mean_factorized the existing factorized_product representation, apart from host nondeterminism; any discrepancy must be investigated before causal interpretation.

Implementation: nonempty fine-recency weights have unit total and empty weights zero in every cell. Log weighting raises low-count occupied-bin share in an unequal two-bin witness without introducing new bins or changing action context.

Primary empirical prediction: log_local increases validation AUC over mean_local; improvement specifically due to target-local periods predicts a larger log advantage locally than under factorization. A generic log improvement in both branches supports weighting utility but not target-local attribution.

Utility/cost decision: retention means paired AUC difference versus joint_identity has a user-cluster-bootstrap 95% lower bound above -.0002, with lower measured train time or inference cost. This margin is a newly declared practical criterion, not an externally established tolerance. Target 3 paired seeds before claiming retention; current four-cell screening cannot establish it.

Secondary: log_local should stay near parent train/wall cost and below frozen joint_identity training cost; report AUC/Logloss tradeoffs, full host throughput/latency, parameter counts and memory rather than claiming an unmeasured saving.
falsifiers: Log local fails to improve matched mean AUC or reverses across paired seeds: reject this implementation as a utility improvement; do not reject all cheap compression.
No positive difference-in-differences [log_local-mean_local]-[log_factorized-mean_factorized]: no support for localization-specific saturation, even if both log branches improve.
Generic factorization effects or Logloss-only improvements do not establish the saturation explanation; latest action-age trials already show metric disagreement.

Implementation errors exceeding predeclared FP32 tolerances invalidate interpretation until repaired: 1e-4 absolute for count/margin identities; 1e-5 for normalized weights, context/dense identity comparisons and padding/reversal invariance; empty outputs should be exactly zero. Mean context versus the copied parent formula should be bitwise equal because the arithmetic is identical. These checks are candidate-authored, limited to the host first-512 batch, and do not replace population uncertainty.
Measured cost increases erase training/inference savings or the declared retention interval fails: no retained-utility efficiency claim.
alternative_explanations: Optimization, stochastic initialization and validation selection across many trajectories; single seed effects remain preliminary.
Unit mass controls total weight but does not match recency vector norm, gradient conditioning or effective regularization; log-versus-mean effects can reflect any of these.
Concavity depends on group size and changes per-group shape even after normalization; explicit group counts remain available and can interact with the head.
Factorized tables contain fractional counts; log then normalization acts differently on fractional mixtures, so factorial interaction does not uniquely identify behavioral causality.

Already-successful local fine recency and nonlinear explicit coarse counts can make the new summary redundant. Target-match groups and coarse category-brand conjunctions remain; this does not isolate all identity pairing.
Static snapshot as-of dates are undocumented; results apply to this frozen benchmark and 128-event supplied prefix, not verified production temporal features.
